name: Chiang Ts’ai-p’in
bio: Chiang Ts'ai-p'in (Jiang Caipin), known as Mei Fei, the "Plum-Blossom" concubine, was a favourite of the T'ang emperor Ming Huang before Yang Kuei-fei supplanted her. The date above is the one Ayscough and Lowell's Contents gives.
The archive holds one poem from Fir-Flower Tablets (1921), the thank-you for a gift of pearls that is traditionally attributed to her.

poems.title: A Letter of Thanks for Precious Pearls Bestowed by One Above
poems.author: Chiang Ts’ai-p’in
poems.note: In the book: the "Plum-Blossom" concubine of the Emperor Ming Huang.
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
It is long--long--since my two eyebrows were painted like cassia-leaves.
I have ended the adorning of myself. My tears soak my dress of coarse red silk.
All day I sit in the Palace of the High Gate. I do not wash; I do not comb my hair.
How can precious pearls soothe so desolate a grief.
